soundness_flags.label: thm:minimax-length-frontier and oeq:exact-minimax-constant
soundness_flags.one_line: Both call P|I| or P|J| “expected length,” although P is a law and interval length is random; replace these objectives with E_{P,Pi}|I| and E_{P,Pi}|J| throughout.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes potential outcomes independent of the action-delay pair, hence conditional outcome-delay independence, and Corollary 4.4 assumes pi_t(a) >= C t^{-alpha} with a polynomial delay-tail condition.
Rewards and delays are generated independently within each arm; Assumption 1 imposes a uniform armwise polynomial delay-tail bound.
The article treats reward-dependent and reward-independent delays and gives near-optimal regret algorithms, including unrestricted and possibly infinite delays.
The article studies strongly reward-dependent delays and establishes regret upper and matching lower bounds for bounded or sub-Gaussian rewards, not confidence-interval coverage.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Repair the minimax and OEQ objectives to use expectation, then state explicitly whether expectation is over both arrivals and adaptive-design randomization.

Add a formal finite-sample or asymptotic lower-bound corollary isolating the hidden-tail two-point experiment from the sampling two-point experiment, including its observable-law equality and divergence calculation.
Sharpen the clinical rule with a worked logged-trial audit protocol that maps an empirical allocation envelope and a justified tail-envelope certification into a concrete follow-up choice.

recommended_next_step: Revise the expected-length notation and then advance this field-tier, novelty-clear kernel to Stage 0.
